policy_title: Streamline infrastructure funding and abolish Net Zero objectives
stated: Reform UK will overhaul and merge the National Infrastructure Commission and the Infrastructure Bank into a single government infrastructure funding stream, simplifying the funding process and abolishing Net Zero objectives to save time, cut waste, and boost funding and accountability.

source.quote: A Single Government Infrastructure Funding Stream Overhaul and merge the National Infrastructure Commission and the Infrastructure Bank. Scrap Net Zero objectives. Simplify the funding process to save time, cut waste, boost funding and accountability.

bearing_set.reason: Abolishing Net Zero objectives is a direct, material intervention in the UK's emissions-reduction framework, with a plausible non-negligible effect on the country's climate and clean-environment trajectory.

Energy infrastructure investment decisions drive long-run household energy costs (a core O2 indicator); removing Net Zero objectives redirects funding away from renewables toward conventional infrastructure, creating a plausible — if contested — effect on energy bills over time.

Redirecting the Infrastructure Bank's ~£22bn mandate away from Net Zero investment and merging governance structures materially changes which productive assets get funded; both the efficiency claim (less duplication) and the investment-mix shift (green to non-green) bear on long-run productivity and living standards — genuinely contested in direction but non-negligible in scale.

membership_note: O6 is the primary bearing: abolishing Net Zero objectives is a direct policy instrument on the emissions and clean-energy pathway. O13 is included because the scale of infrastructure capital reallocation and the claimed efficiency gains both plausibly move productivity/living-standards indicators over the medium term. Fiscal/O12 effects are possible but the Infrastructure Bank operates as an investment vehicle, not a direct spending line, so no specific funded-vs-borrowed mechanism can be pinned to the merger alone. O2 (energy prices) and O5 (energy security) effects are too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
